Description: 1. DESCRIPTION:As a Product Owner, I want a finalized, versioned API contract between Five9 and IO for exchanging interaction/call data so that both systems can reliably create, update, and retrieve call outcomes, dispositions, and related metadata for reporting, analytics, and member engagement workflows.Scope of Contract :POST (Five9 → IO): Persist completed interaction records (call outcomes, disposition, attempts, timestamps, source system).GET (IO → Compass): Retrieve interaction records by UUID, by member/date range, or by opportunity.Core Business Outcomes:Ensure data consistency across Five9 and IO.Enable near real-time availability of interaction data for downstream systems (e.g., Compass UI, analytics).Reduce ambiguity by agreeing on required vs. optional fields, data types, max lengths, and time zone/format conventions.2. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS:Performance:POST (single record): ≤ 500 ms P95.GET (single record): ≤ 300 ms P95; GET (list ≤ 100 records): ≤ 800 ms P95.Availability: 99.9% monthly uptime; graceful error responses.Security: OAuth 2.0 (client credentials) or mTLS; TLS 1.2+; RBAC scopes.Compliance: HIPAA/PHI alignment where applicable; audit logging of all calls.Reliability: Idempotent POST using uuid/dedup keys; retry guidance for transient failures.Observability: Structured logs with correlation IDs; metrics (latency, error rates); tracing.Versioning: Semantic versioning (v1); backward-compatible additions; deprecation policy with notice.Data Quality Controls: Validation of required fields, data types, and max lengths; dateTime normalized to Central Time (CT) with agreed format (ISO 8601 + offset).Rate Limiting: Per-client limits; 429 with Retry-After.Documentation: OpenAPI/Swagger specs with request/response samples and error catalog.3. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:Scenario #1: Finalize POST Contract (Five9 → IO)Given Five9 needs to persist an interaction record after a callWhen Five9 sends a POST /v1/interactions with all required fieldsThen IO responds with 201 Created, echoes uuid, and stores the record with all fields validated (types/lengths) and dateTime recorded in CT.Required fields (illustrative and adjustable during contract finalization):uuid (STRING, ≤ 50) — unique call/interaction IDdateTime (DATETIME, CT, ISO 8601)programType (STRING, ≤ 50)memberIdType (STRING, ≤ 20)memberId (STRING, ≤ 50)interactionType (STRING, ≤ 50)opportunityId (STRING, ≤ 50)opportunityType (STRING, ≤ 50)opportunitySubType (STRING, ≤ 50)disposition (STRING, ≤ 50)sourceSystem (STRING, ≤ 50; e.g., Five9)Optional fields:interactionSubType (STRING, ≤ 50)phoneNumber (STRING, ≤ 50)attemptCount (INTEGER)Scenario #2: Finalize GET Contract (IO → Five9/Compass)Given a consumer needs to retrieve interactions for a member within a date rangeWhen the consumer calls GET /v1/interactions?memberId={memberId}&dateFrom={ISO}&dateTo={ISO}&page={n}&pageSize={m}Then the API returns 200 OK with a list of interaction records adhering to the same contract, sorted by dateTimedescending, and includes pagination metadata (page, pageSize, total, hasNext).4. DEMO CRITERIA:Contract Walkthrough: Review OpenAPI spec showing field definitions, required vs. optional, max lengths, and examples.POST Demo:Send a valid POST payload; verify 201 Created, stored data integrity, and logs with correlation ID.GET Demo:Retrieve by uuid and by memberId + date range; verify payload structure, sorting, and pagination.Observability Check: Show metrics and traces for the above calls; confirm security (token validation / mTLS).5. ASSUMPTIONS:Five9 will produce uuid or a deterministic key suitable for idempotency.IO will act as the system of record for persisted interaction data exposed to consumers.Time normalization is to Central Time (CT) using ISO 8601 with offset (e.g., 2026-01-05T15:30:00-06:00).6. DEPENDENCIES:Five9 team: Endpoint integration, payload production (POST), contract alignment on dispositions and interaction taxonomy.IO team: API implementation (POST/GET), data validation, storage/indexing, pagination, sorting, and OpenAPI ownership.Compass/Consumer Apps: UI mapping (display fields), pagination handling, error rendering.
